key_insight: A generalized safety measure can be learned directly from large-scale, unlabeled naturalistic driving data to predict collision and near-crash risk in real time, giving vehicles extra time for early reactions.
problem_solved: How to detect and warn about collision risk reliably without relying on scarce, manually labeled crash data, enabling scalable safety assessment from everyday driving behavior.
method: Train a risk estimator from large-scale naturalistic driving streams using unlabeled / self-supervised signals and surrogate near-miss patterns.
Model produces a generalized collision-risk score that runs in real time to flag impending crashes and near-crashes.
Validate the approach at scale against naturalistic crash and near-crash occurrences to demonstrate earlier and more accurate warnings than baseline metrics.
impact: Enables AI/ML teams to build and evaluate safety predictors using abundant unlabeled driving data, reducing dependence on rare labeled crashes and improving early-warning capabilities for ADAS and autonomous vehicles.
visual_elements: Timeline diagram showing how the learned risk score rises before crash/near-crash, highlighting extra lead time for reaction.
Overlay visualization: driving scene with color-coded risk heatmap on nearby agents (low→high risk).
Performance chart comparing detection lead time and accuracy vs. baseline metrics (e.g., precision/recall or time-to-warning).
Schematic pipeline: naturalistic data → self-supervised risk learning → real-time risk estimator → early warning loop.
paper_title: Learning collision risk proactively from naturalistic driving data at scale
paper_authors: Yiru Jiao, Simeon C. Calvert, Sander van Cranenburgh, Hans van Lint
